message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that’s actually scheduled on a regular cycle.  In practice, the tower is repainted every **seven years** to protect its iron structure from corrosion.  The actual work—spraying the metal, cleaning, priming, and applying the final coats—takes roughly **two months**.

Here’s why:

| Factor | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Height** | 324 m (1,063 ft) |
| **Surface area** | ~10 000 m² (about 107 000 ft²) |
| **Paint required** | ~60 tons (≈ 27 000 kg) of protective paint |
| **Workers** | 30–40 skilled painters plus support crew |
| **Equipment** | 12–15 scaffolding towers, 4–5 paint‑spray rigs, 2–3 cranes for heavy lifts |
| **Time per phase** | 1–2 weeks for cleaning & priming, 1–2 weeks for top‑coat application, 1–2 weeks for finishing touches and inspection |

So, if you’re planning a one‑off project, expect about **8–10 weeks** of continuous work, assuming you have the necessary permits, equipment, and a crew ready to work at heights. If you’re just curious about the routine maintenance, the tower’s official schedule keeps it fresh every **seven years**, with each repaint lasting around **two months**.
